summary.short: Amends the Illinois Right of Publicity Act (765 ILCS 1075), effective 1 January 2025, to define AI and digital replica terms and prohibit distributing works containing unauthorized digital replicas, with post-mortem and intermediary provisions.
summary.long: House Bill 4875 amends Sections 5, 20, 30 and 35 of the Illinois Right of Publicity Act, effective 1/1/2025. Section 5 adds definitions of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, digital replica and unauthorized digital replica, and defines person, service provider and individual. Section 20 lists who may enforce the rights, including the individual, transferees and, after death, persons with an interest in the rights. Section 30 bars commercial use of an individual's identity during life without written consent (subsection a); bars knowing distribution or making available to the public of a sound recording or audiovisual work with actual knowledge that it contains an unauthorized digital replica (b); extends the commercial-use restriction to a deceased individual's identity or digital replica for 50 years after death where death occurs after the effective date (c); makes a person who materially contributes to or facilitates a violation liable after obtaining actual knowledge (d); exempts certain transmitting, storing and hosting providers that lack knowledge or remove material expeditiously on notice (e); and incorporates 17 U.S.C. 512 elements and 47 U.S.C. 230 (f, g). Section 35 applies the Act to acts or events after the effective date, lists exemptions for live performances, news, political campaigns, documentaries and parody, and excludes actions filed or pending before the effective date.}},

relations.note: Amends Sections 5, 20, 30 and 35 of the Act. The supplied text does not mark which wording is new.

evidence.quote: The Right of Publicity Act is amended by changing Sections 5, 20, 30, and 35 as follows:

relations.note: Section 30(f) incorporates all elements of 17 U.S.C. 512 for claims about unauthorized digital replicas, subject to Section 30(e).

evidence.quote: all of the elements of 17 U.S.C. 512 shall be incorporated mutatis mutandis with respect to claims relating to unauthorized digital replicas.

relations.note: Section 30(e) gives the meaning of "expeditiously" by reference to 17 U.S.C. 512 for the service-provider safe harbour.

evidence.quote: "expeditiously" has the same meaning as it does in 17 U.S.C. 512.

relations.note: Section 30(g) provides that nothing in the Act may be construed inconsistently with 47 U.S.C. 230 or other federal law.

evidence.quote: Nothing in this Act may be construed in a manner inconsistent with 47 U.S.C. 230 or any other federal law.

relations.note: The definition of "Cloud service provider" adopts the federal definition by reference. Section 30(e) refers to cloud service providers.

evidence.quote: "Cloud service provider" means a cloud service provider as defined by 6 U.S.C. 650.

relations.note: The definition of "Service provider" refers to a wireless carrier as defined in 47 U.S.C. 615b(4).

evidence.quote: a wireless carrier as defined by 47 U.S.C. 615b(4)

relations.note: The definition of "Service provider" uses the term "broadband service" as defined in Section 10 of the Broadband Advisory Council Act.

evidence.quote: any entity offering broadband service as that term is used in Section 10 of the Broadband Advisory Council Act

relations.note: The definition of "Service provider" uses the term "telecommunication carrier" as used in Section 13-202 of the Public Utilities Act.

evidence.quote: a telecommunication carrier as that term is used in Section 13-202 of the Public Utilities Act

relations.target_text: Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Law of the Civil Administrative Code of Illinois
relations.note: The definition of "Person" excludes a data center as defined in this law from liability under Section 30(b) and (d).

evidence.quote: does not include a data center, as defined by the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Law of the Civil Administrative Code of Illinois

notes: Section 35(b) reads "Subsections (a) and (c) of Section 30 do This Act does not apply to the following:", which appears to be a drafting artefact (a missing verb or deleted words). Section 35(c) then refers to subsections (b) and (c) of Section 30, so the scope of the exclusions is internally inconsistent. The supplied text does not mark insertions or deletions, so the new wording cannot be separated from restated text. The footer gives an effective date of 1/1/2025, which the text does not state in its operative provisions. Section 35(d) excludes actions filed or pending before the amendatory Act's effective date. Section 30(c) refers to deaths after the Act's effective date.

"Artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.
"Commercial purpose" means the public use or holding out of an individual's identity
"Application software provider" means a person providing a digital distribution service for other software applications
"Cloud service provider" means a cloud service provider as defined by 6 U.S.C. 650.

"Digital replica" means a newly created, electronic representation of the voice, image, or likeness of an actual individual created using a computer, algorithm, software, tool, artificial intelligence, or other technology
"Identity" means any attribute of an individual that serves to identify that individual to an ordinary, reasonable viewer or listener
"Individual" means a living or deceased natural person
"Juristic person" means a partnership, trust, estate, corporation, unincorporated association, or other organization capable of suing and being sued in a court of law.
"Name" means the actual name or other name by which an individual is known that is intended to identify that individual.
"Person" means a natural or juristic person.

"Person" does not include a data center, as defined by the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Law of the Civil Administrative Code of Illinois, under subsections (b) and (d) of Section 30.
"Service provider" means any entity offering broadband service as that term is used in Section 10 of the Broadband Advisory Council Act
"Unauthorized digital replica" means the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the appropriate person or persons identified in Section 20
"Work of Fine Art" means (i) a visual rendition including, but not limited to, a painting, drawing, sculpture, mosaic, videotape, or photograph

obligations.summary: A person (natural or juristic) may not use an individual's identity for commercial purposes during the individual's lifetime without prior written consent (Sec. 30(a)). Sec. 30(c) extends the same consent requirement to use of the identity or a digital replica for commercial purposes for 50 years after death.
obligations.applies_from: Effective date 1/1/2025; Sec. 35(a) applies the Act to acts or events after its effective date
obligations.conditional_on: Use for commercial purposes as defined in Sec. 5; Sec. 35(b) exemptions apply to Sec. 30(a) and (c)

evidence.quote: A person may not use an individual's identity for commercial purposes during the individual's lifetime without having obtained previous written consent

obligations.summary: A person may not knowingly distribute, transmit, or make available to the general public a sound recording or audiovisual work with actual knowledge that it contains an unauthorized digital replica.
obligations.applies_from: Effective date 1/1/2025; Sec. 35(a) applies the Act to acts or events after its effective date
obligations.conditional_on: Actual knowledge that the work contains an unauthorized digital replica; Sec. 35(c) exemptions apply to Sec. 30(b)

evidence.quote: A person may not knowingly distribute, transmit, or make available to the general public a sound recording or audiovisual work with actual knowledge that the work contains an unauthorized digital replica.

obligations.summary: Each person who enforces rights as a successor under Sec. 20(a)(3) (after death of an individual who has not transferred rights) must make a proportional accounting to, and act in good faith toward, other persons in whom the enforced rights have vested.
obligations.conditional_on: Enforcement of rights under Sec. 20(a)(3) after the individual's death

evidence.quote: shall make a proportional accounting to, and shall act at all times in good faith with respect to, any other person in whom the rights being enforced have vested.
